formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future; a leader rejects transfer/step-down admission, assigns index and term, stores the batch, then reports its own match. Ordinary follower append rejects old term or predecessor mismatch, truncates conflicting suffix and stores before success. Ordinary and pipeline replication report successful nonempty request boundaries to their captured commitment; snapshot transfer reports the finalized/restored snapshot boundary. Commitment keeps only latest voters, takes a majority order statistic, and advances only at or beyond the leader startIndex. Leader commit notification records commitment/configuration and queues the committed prefix to the FSM. Commands complete after single/batch application; barriers pass through the same worker; no-ops can finish without an FSM callback. Error checks differ between ordinary transport and pipeline future consumption, retained as a local contract lead rather than an assumed valid report.

context.explanation: Startup reads stable term/log tail, installs snapshot metadata and normally restores FSM, then scans later configuration entries before workers start. Bootstrap seeds clean state; forced RecoverCluster and Restore explicitly permit disaster-recovery replacement. Follower contact timeout and latest voter eligibility enter candidacy. Optional pre-vote tests proposed authority without persisting term, then real election persists term/self-vote and counts voter-targeted replies on campaign-local channels. Receivers enforce term, known-leader, candidate eligibility, prior-vote and history-order checks. Higher-term requests/replies, inadequate recent voter contact, negative verification or committed self-removal can cause authority loss. Transfer waits for target replication progress then TimeoutNow starts a normal majority election with transfer exceptions. Independent heartbeats refresh contact and verification separately from durable log support. F-elected-role records only the local quorum-tally transition; the main dispatcher subsequently consumes local Leader state to enter runLeader, subject to shutdown.

connection.explanation: Each leadership generation creates zeroed voter matches and startIndex=lastIndex+1, dispatches a no-op, and gives workers the generation commitment pointer and step-down channel. Exit stops workers and fails remaining inflight/verification futures; already committed FSM tuples survive on their serialized queue. Durable prior logs constrain new elections by term/index freshness, but need fresh generation support before commitment. Configuration changes require the prior configuration and a current-term entry committed; latest configuration immediately changes voter filtering, preserving matches by continuing ID. Snapshot creation binds an applied FSM boundary to a committed configuration before log compaction, while startup/installation restores those contexts. User Restore aborts remaining inflight work, serializes restoration after queued FSM work and burns a log index so subsequent replication uses the snapshot; its special recovery contract is distinct from normal preservation. The local role transition is the explicit connection from the election owner to fresh leader-generation initialization, not an assumed global leadership guarantee.

formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future. Leader admission checks transfer and step-down, dispatch assigns index/term and stores locally before reporting self support. context.explanation: Startup reads stable term/log tail, installs snapshot metadata and normally restores FSM, then scans later configuration entries before workers start. Bootstrap seeds clean state; forced RecoverCluster and Restore explicitly permit disaster-recovery replacement. Follower contact timeout and latest voter eligibility enter candidacy. Optional pre-vote tests proposed authority without persisting term, then real election persists term/self-vote and counts voter-targeted replies on campaign-local channels. Receivers enforce term, known-leader, candidate eligibility, prior-vote and history-order checks. Higher-term requests/replies, inadequate recent voter contact, negative verification or committed self-removal can cause authority loss. Transfer waits for target replication progress then TimeoutNow starts a normal majority election with transfer exceptions. Independent heartbeats refresh contact and verification separately from durable log support. F-elected-role records only the local quorum-tally transition; the main dispatcher subsequently consumes local Leader state to enter runLeader, subject to shutdown.

connection.explanation: Each leadership generation creates zeroed voter matches and startIndex=lastIndex+1, dispatches a no-op, and gives workers the generation commitment pointer and step-down channel. Exit stops workers and fails remaining inflight/verification futures; already committed FSM tuples survive on their serialized queue. Durable prior logs constrain new elections by term/index freshness, but need fresh generation support before commitment. Configuration changes require the prior configuration and a current-term entry committed; latest configuration immediately changes voter filtering, preserving matches by continuing ID. Snapshot creation binds an applied FSM boundary to a committed configuration before log compaction, while startup/installation restores those contexts. User Restore aborts remaining inflight work, serializes restoration after queued FSM work and burns a log index so subsequent replication uses the snapshot; its special recovery contract is distinct from normal preservation. The local role transition is the explicit connection from the election owner to fresh leader-generation initialization, not an assumed global leadership guarantee.

latest_decision.rationale: Explore the concrete two-write boundary without claiming a consensus violation or applicable crash guarantee. Bootstrap and actual processRPC handlers create all critical receiver state; messages are controlled inputs rather than real remote elections. Background workers are omitted via the existing skipStartup test option, so full concurrent protocol reachability remains open. The StableStore wrapper fails one candidate-byte Set before mutation and otherwise delegates; a no-fault control uses the same receiver sequence. This experiment tests local failure/retry semantics only, not an obligation or system safety.
